audience: A 27-year-old designer in Bengaluru who works out of cafés and airport lounges, lives out of one backpack, and whose laptop always dies at 2 %.
insight: The charger is always in the bag, just never where the hand goes: a black bag is a black hole, and you dig through it blind while the battery hits 2 %.
smp: In the Transit Z, time spent digging is zero seconds.
device: zips: in the dark of a black-hole bag a torch beam hunts for the charger; on the bass a zip rips the dark open into Mokobara yellow, and each compartment then opens with its own zip and its item is found in 0 sec
device_why: the product's whole promise is compartments you unzip and find things in at once, so every cut is a zip opening one compartment, and the dark-to-yellow rip is the lining itself

recall.does: its own pocket for the charger, cards, keys and phone: 0 sec digging
recall.why: you find anything in the bag instantly, even when the laptop is at 2 %

claims.text: Time spent digging = 0 seconds; the suspended charger pocket helps you find your tech essentials ASAP, so you can plug in your laptop before it dies
claims.source: Mokobara's own Transit Z film (product page video, cdn.shopify.com …90428710.mp4)

claims.text: front bucket compartment with a key holder and cardholder
secret magnetic pocket for passport, boarding pass and cellphone
₹6,299; 30 litres; fits up to a 15.6-inch laptop

music.title: Big Dawgs
music.why: the Kerala rapper's global Reels anthem: a swaggering track for a bag that has its life sorted; the preview's quiet open gives the dark hook 2.3 s, then the 808 lands exactly when the zip rips the dark open

look.why: Mokobara's own yellow (measured off its mailer box): the colour of the Transit Z lining, so the whole reel lives inside the bag; the hook alone is black (the black-hole bag), and every shot is keyed off its white studio sweep onto the yellow
